title: Nodal & Mesh Analysis
description: Node voltages and mesh currents as phasors in circuits with several sources, current sources and dependent sources.

study.title: Node analysis with phasors
study.body: Pick a reference node, label the unknown node voltage phasors and write KCL at each one: the current leaving through an impedance $Z$ to node $k$ is $(\mathbf{V}_n - \mathbf{V}_k)/Z$. Admittances are handy: $j\omega C$ for a capacitor and $1/(j\omega L) = -j/(\omega L)$ for an inductor. Solve the complex linear system (substitution or Cramer's rule).

study.title: Sources and their phasors
study.body: All sources must share one frequency. Cosines map directly to $V_m\angle\theta$; a sine first becomes a cosine: $\sin(\omega t + \alpha) = \cos(\omega t + \alpha - 90^\circ)$. A voltage source between two non-reference nodes forms a **supernode**: one KCL for both nodes plus $\mathbf{V}_b - \mathbf{V}_a = \mathbf{V}_s$.

study.title: Dependent sources
study.body: Keep the dependent source in every equation, as if it were independent with value gain × control. Then add one equation that expresses the control variable in the unknowns, e.g. $\mathbf{I}_x = (\mathbf{V}_s - \mathbf{V}_a)/R_1$. Never zero it.

study.title: Mesh analysis
study.body: Assign clockwise mesh currents and write KVL around each mesh with impedances. An element shared by meshes 1 and 2 carries $\mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{I}_2$; a current source in an outer branch sets that mesh current directly.

study.title: Common mistakes
study.body:
- Writing a sine source as $V_m\angle\alpha$ instead of $V_m\angle(\alpha - 90^\circ)$.
- Using $j\omega C$ as an impedance (it is the admittance).
- Subtracting amplitudes for a shared branch: the current is the phasor $\mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{I}_2$.
- Adding phasors of sources with **different** frequencies: use superposition in the time domain.

steps.prompt: $v_1(t) = {{V1}}\cos({{w}}t)$ V and $v_2(t) = {{V2}}\cos({{w}}t + \theta_2)$ V with $\theta_2$ = {{th2}}° (same frequency). Use node analysis.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of the node voltage $v_a$.
ask.explanation: KCL at a: $\frac{\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_1}{R} + j\omega C\,\mathbf{V}_a + \frac{\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_2}{j\omega L} = 0$, so $\mathbf{V}_a = \frac{\mathbf{V}_1/R + \mathbf{V}_2/(j\omega L)}{1/R + j(\omega C - 1/\omega L)}$. The denominator is {{G|S}} + j({{B|S}}). Result: $\mathbf{V}_a$ = **{{v_a|V}}** ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $v_a$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: $\mathbf{V}_a = \frac{\mathbf{V}_1/R + \mathbf{V}_2/(j\omega L)}{1/R + j(\omega C - 1/\omega L)}$ with $\mathbf{V}_1$ = {{V1}}∠0° V, $\mathbf{V}_2$ = {{V2}}∠{{th2}}° V, and the denominator {{G|S}} + j({{B|S}}). Result: {{v_a|V}} ∠ **{{v_a_ph|°}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of the current through $C$.
ask.explanation: Node analysis gives $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}. Then $|\mathbf{I}_C| = \omega C\,|\mathbf{V}_a|$ = {{w*C|S}} · {{v_a|V}} = **{{I_C1|A}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of the current through $L$.
ask.explanation: With $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}: $\mathbf{I}_L = \frac{\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_2}{j\omega L}$, and $|\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_2|$ = {{I_L1*w*L|V}}, so $|\mathbf{I}_L|$ = {{I_L1*w*L|V}} / {{w*L|Ω}} = **{{I_L1|A}}**.

steps.require: min(v_b - 0.05*Vm, 1.5*Vm - v_a, 1.5*Vm - v_b, abs(v_b_ph - th) - 5, abs(v_a_ph - th) - 5)
steps.prompt: $v_s(t) = {{Vm}}\cos({{w}}t + \theta)$ V with $\theta$ = {{th}}°. Use node analysis with the reference node shown.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_a$.
ask.explanation: KCL at a: $\frac{\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_s}{R_1} + \frac{\mathbf{V}_a}{j\omega L} + j\omega C(\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_b) = 0$. KCL at b: $j\omega C(\mathbf{V}_b - \mathbf{V}_a) + \frac{\mathbf{V}_b}{R_2} = 0$. With $1/\omega L$ = {{YL|S}} and $\omega C$ = {{YC|S}}, solving gives $\mathbf{V}_a$ = **{{v_a|V}}** ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $v_b$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: From KCL at b: $\mathbf{V}_b = \mathbf{V}_a\frac{j\omega CR_2}{1 + j\omega CR_2}$, which leads $\mathbf{V}_a$ by $90^\circ - \arctan(\omega CR_2)$ = {{90-deg(atan(YC*R2))|°}}. Solving both equations: $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}, so $\mathbf{V}_b$ = {{v_b|V}} ∠ **{{v_b_ph|°}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_b$.
ask.explanation: Solving the two KCL equations gives $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}. Node b is a divider of $\mathbf{V}_a$: $|\mathbf{V}_b| = |\mathbf{V}_a|\frac{\omega CR_2}{\sqrt{1 + (\omega CR_2)^2}}$ = **{{v_b|V}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of the current through $C$.
ask.explanation: $\mathbf{I}_C = j\omega C(\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_b)$, which is also the current in $R_2$: $|\mathbf{I}_C| = |\mathbf{V}_b|/R_2$ = {{v_b|V}} / {{R2|Ω}} = **{{I_C1|A}}**.

steps.prompt: $v_s(t) = {{Vm}}\cos({{w}}t)$ V and $i_s(t) = {{Im*1000}}\cos({{w}}t + \varphi)$ mA with $\varphi$ = {{phi}}°.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_b$.
ask.explanation: KCL at a: $\frac{\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_s}{R_1} + j\omega C\mathbf{V}_a + \frac{\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_b}{R_2} = 0$. KCL at b (the source current enters b): $\frac{\mathbf{V}_b - \mathbf{V}_a}{R_2} + \frac{\mathbf{V}_b}{j\omega L} = \mathbf{I}_s$. Solving: $\mathbf{V}_b$ = **{{v_b|V}}** ∠ {{v_b_ph|°}} (and $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}).

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $v_b$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: Write KCL at a and b (with $\mathbf{I}_s$ = {{Im*1000}}∠{{phi}}° mA entering b), then solve the 2×2 complex system: $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}, $\mathbf{V}_b$ = {{v_b|V}} ∠ **{{v_b_ph|°}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_a$.
ask.explanation: KCL at a and b, solved together: $\mathbf{V}_a$ = **{{v_a|V}}** ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}, $\mathbf{V}_b$ = {{v_b|V}} ∠ {{v_b_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of the current through $R_2$.
ask.explanation: $\mathbf{I}_{R_2} = (\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_b)/R_2$ with $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}} and $\mathbf{V}_b$ = {{v_b|V}} ∠ {{v_b_ph|°}}: subtract in rectangular form, $|\mathbf{I}_{R_2}|$ = **{{I_R2|A}}**.

steps.prompt: Put the steps of phasor node-voltage analysis in order.
items: Convert every source to a phasor (same $\omega$) and every R, L, C to an impedance
Choose the reference node and label the unknown node voltages
Write KCL at each unknown node with currents $(\mathbf{V}_n - \mathbf{V}_k)/Z$
Compute the requested branch currents and convert back to time functions
steps.explanation: It is the DC method with complex numbers. Voltage sources connected to the reference fix a node voltage directly; a floating voltage source needs a supernode.

steps.prompt: Which equation is KCL at node a (currents leaving a)?
steps.explanation: Each current leaving a is (voltage difference)/impedance. For $C$ that is $\mathbf{V}_a/(1/j\omega C) = j\omega C\,\mathbf{V}_a$; for $L$ it is $(\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_2)/(j\omega L)$. The other options multiply by an impedance instead of dividing, or flip the sign of one leaving current.

steps.prompt: $v_s(t) = {{Vm}}\cos({{w}}t + \theta)$ V with $\theta$ = {{th}}°. Three unknown nodes a, b, c.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_c$.
ask.explanation: KCL at a: $\frac{\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_s}{R_1} + j\omega C_1\mathbf{V}_a + \frac{\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_b}{j\omega L} = 0$; at b: $\frac{\mathbf{V}_b - \mathbf{V}_a}{j\omega L} + \frac{\mathbf{V}_b}{R_2} + j\omega C_2(\mathbf{V}_b - \mathbf{V}_c) = 0$; at c: $j\omega C_2(\mathbf{V}_c - \mathbf{V}_b) + \frac{\mathbf{V}_c}{R_3} = 0$. Solving: $\mathbf{V}_c$ = **{{v_c|V}}** ∠ {{v_c_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $v_c$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: Solve the three KCL equations (a, b, c): $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}, $\mathbf{V}_b$ = {{v_b|V}} ∠ {{v_b_ph|°}}, $\mathbf{V}_c$ = {{v_c|V}} ∠ **{{v_c_ph|°}}**. Check: c is an RC divider of b, so it leads $\mathbf{V}_b$ by $90^\circ - \arctan(\omega C_2 R_3)$ = {{90-deg(atan(w*C2*R3))|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_b$.
ask.explanation: Solve KCL at a, b and c together: $\mathbf{V}_b$ = **{{v_b|V}}** ∠ {{v_b_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of the current through $L$.
ask.explanation: Solving KCL at a, b, c gives $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}} and $\mathbf{V}_b$ = {{v_b|V}} ∠ {{v_b_ph|°}}. $|\mathbf{I}_L| = |\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_b|/(\omega L)$ = **{{I_L1|A}}**.

steps.prompt: $v_1(t) = {{V1}}\cos({{w}}t)$ V and $v_2(t) = {{V2}}\sin({{w}}t)$ V. Note the **sine**.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $v_a$ in degrees (cosine reference).
ask.explanation: First convert: $\sin(\omega t) = \cos(\omega t - 90^\circ)$, so $\mathbf{V}_2$ = {{V2}}∠−90° V = −j{{V2}} V. KCL at a: $\mathbf{V}_a = \frac{\mathbf{V}_1/R + \mathbf{V}_2/(j\omega L)}{1/R + j(\omega C - 1/\omega L)}$, denominator {{G|S}} + j({{B|S}}). Result: {{v_a|V}} ∠ **{{v_a_ph|°}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_a$.
ask.explanation: $\mathbf{V}_2$ = {{V2}}∠−90° V (sine → cosine with −90°). $\mathbf{V}_a = \frac{\mathbf{V}_1/R + \mathbf{V}_2/(j\omega L)}{1/R + j(\omega C - 1/\omega L)}$ = **{{v_a|V}}** ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}.

steps.prompt: A circuit has a 50 Hz source and a 150 Hz source. You can find a node voltage by writing one set of phasor node equations with both sources in it.
steps.explanation: A phasor carries one frequency, and the impedances $j\omega L$, $1/(j\omega C)$ differ per frequency. Use **superposition**: solve the circuit once per source (with its own $\omega$), convert each result back to a time function, and add the time functions — never the phasors.

steps.prompt: Amplifier model: $v_s(t) = {{Vm}}\cos({{w}}t)$ V, and the VCCS draws $g\,v_x$ downward with $g$ = {{g*1000}} mS, where $v_x$ is the voltage across $C$.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_{out}$.
ask.explanation: KCL at x: $\frac{\mathbf{V}_x - \mathbf{V}_s}{R_1} + j\omega C\mathbf{V}_x + \frac{\mathbf{V}_x - \mathbf{V}_{out}}{R_f} = 0$. KCL at out: $\frac{\mathbf{V}_{out} - \mathbf{V}_x}{R_f} + g\mathbf{V}_x + \frac{\mathbf{V}_{out}}{R_2} = 0$. Solving: $\mathbf{V}_x$ = {{v_v_x|V}} ∠ {{v_v_x_ph|°}}, $\mathbf{V}_{out}$ = **{{v_v_out|V}}** ∠ {{v_v_out_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $v_{out}$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: Solve the two KCL equations (x and out) with the dependent current $g\mathbf{V}_x$ leaving node out: $\mathbf{V}_{out}$ = {{v_v_out|V}} ∠ **{{v_v_out_ph|°}}**. Roughly $\mathbf{V}_{out} \approx -gR_2\mathbf{V}_x$ (inverting, about 180° from $\mathbf{V}_x$ = {{v_v_x|V}} ∠ {{v_v_x_ph|°}}); $R_f$ modifies this.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_x$.
ask.explanation: Writing KCL at x and out and solving the 2×2 system: $\mathbf{V}_x$ = **{{v_v_x|V}}** ∠ {{v_v_x_ph|°}}. The feedback resistor $R_f$ couples the output back to x, so you cannot treat the input as a plain RC divider.

steps.prompt: $v_s(t) = {{Vm}}\cos({{w}}t + \theta)$ V with $\theta$ = {{th}}°. The CCVS (+ at the top) produces $r\,i_x$ with $r$ = {{r}} Ω.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_a$.
ask.explanation: KCL at a: $\frac{\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_s}{R_1} + j\omega C\mathbf{V}_a + \frac{\mathbf{V}_a - r\mathbf{I}_x}{j\omega L} = 0$, with the control equation $\mathbf{I}_x = \frac{\mathbf{V}_s - \mathbf{V}_a}{R_1}$. Substituting and solving: $\mathbf{V}_a$ = **{{v_a|V}}** ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $v_a$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: Replace $\mathbf{I}_x$ by $(\mathbf{V}_s - \mathbf{V}_a)/R_1$ in KCL at a, collect the $\mathbf{V}_a$ terms and solve: $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ **{{v_a_ph|°}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $i_x$.
ask.explanation: After solving for $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}: $\mathbf{I}_x = (\mathbf{V}_s - \mathbf{V}_a)/R_1$, amplitude **{{I_R1|A}}**.

steps.prompt: A circuit contains a dependent source $\beta\,\mathbf{I}_x$. How do you handle it in node analysis?
options: Treat it as a source in KCL and add an equation for $\mathbf{I}_x$ in terms of the node voltages
Set it to zero while writing KCL, then add its effect at the end
Use superposition: one solution with only the dependent source active
steps.explanation: A dependent source stays in the circuit in every step: write KCL as if it were an independent source with value $\beta\mathbf{I}_x$, then express the control variable ($\mathbf{I}_x$, or a voltage $\mathbf{V}_x$) in the node-voltage unknowns. It can never be switched off or used alone in superposition, because it cannot drive the circuit by itself.

steps.prompt: Two current sources at the same frequency: $i_1(t) = {{I1*1000}}\cos({{w}}t)$ mA and $i_2(t) = {{I2*1000}}\cos({{w}}t + \varphi)$ mA with $\varphi$ = {{phi}}°.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_a$.
ask.explanation: KCL (sources entering): a: $\frac{\mathbf{V}_a}{R} + j\omega C(\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_b) = \mathbf{I}_1$; b: $j\omega C(\mathbf{V}_b - \mathbf{V}_a) + \frac{\mathbf{V}_b}{j\omega L} = \mathbf{I}_2$. Solving: $\mathbf{V}_a$ = **{{v_a|V}}** ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $v_b$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: Solve the KCL equations at a and b (admittances $1/R$, $j\omega C$ = j{{w*C|S}}, $1/(j\omega L)$ = −j{{1/(w*L)|S}}): $\mathbf{V}_b$ = {{v_b|V}} ∠ **{{v_b_ph|°}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_b$.
ask.explanation: Solving the two KCL equations: $\mathbf{V}_b$ = **{{v_b|V}}** ∠ {{v_b_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of the current through $C$.
ask.explanation: $\mathbf{I}_C = j\omega C(\mathbf{V}_a - \mathbf{V}_b)$ with $\mathbf{V}_a$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}} and $\mathbf{V}_b$ = {{v_b|V}} ∠ {{v_b_ph|°}}: **{{I_C1|A}}**. Check with KCL at a: $\mathbf{I}_C = \mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{V}_a/R$.

steps.prompt: $i_s(t) = {{Im*1000}}\cos({{w}}t)$ mA and the floating source $v_2(t) = {{V2}}\cos({{w}}t + \theta_2)$ V with $\theta_2$ = {{th2}}° (+ on the b side).

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_b$.
ask.explanation: a and b form a **supernode** with $\mathbf{V}_b = \mathbf{V}_a + \mathbf{V}_2$. KCL for the supernode: $j\omega C\mathbf{V}_a + \frac{\mathbf{V}_b}{R} + \frac{\mathbf{V}_b}{j\omega L} = \mathbf{I}_s$. Substitute $\mathbf{V}_a = \mathbf{V}_b - \mathbf{V}_2$ and solve: $\mathbf{V}_b$ = **{{v_b|V}}** ∠ {{v_b_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $v_a$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: Supernode KCL $j\omega C\mathbf{V}_a + (\mathbf{V}_a + \mathbf{V}_2)\left(\frac1R + \frac{1}{j\omega L}\right) = \mathbf{I}_s$ gives $\mathbf{V}_a = \frac{\mathbf{I}_s - \mathbf{V}_2(1/R + 1/j\omega L)}{j\omega C + 1/R + 1/j\omega L}$ = {{v_a|V}} ∠ **{{v_a_ph|°}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_a$.
ask.explanation: $\mathbf{V}_a = \frac{\mathbf{I}_s - \mathbf{V}_2(1/R + 1/j\omega L)}{j\omega C + 1/R + 1/j\omega L}$ = **{{v_a|V}}** ∠ {{v_a_ph|°}} (from the supernode KCL with $\mathbf{V}_b = \mathbf{V}_a + \mathbf{V}_2$).

steps.prompt: $v_s(t) = {{Vm}}\cos({{w}}t + \theta)$ V with $\theta$ = {{th}}°. The CCCS pushes $\beta i_x$ upward with $\beta$ = {{beta}}.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $i_x$.
ask.explanation: The left loop is a series $R_1$, $L$ circuit (the CCCS does not load it): $\mathbf{I}_x = \frac{\mathbf{V}_s}{R_1 + j\omega L}$, $|R_1 + j\omega L|$ = {{sqrt(R1^2+XL^2)|Ω}}, so $|\mathbf{I}_x|$ = **{{I_R1|A}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $v_{out}$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: $\mathbf{V}_{out} = \beta\mathbf{I}_x R_2$ has the phase of $\mathbf{I}_x = \mathbf{V}_s/(R_1 + j\omega L)$: {{th}}° − arctan({{XL|Ω}}/{{R1|Ω}}) = **{{v_v_out_ph|°}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $v_{out}$.
ask.explanation: $|\mathbf{I}_x|$ = {{I_R1|A}}. The dependent current {{beta}} · {{I_R1|A}} = {{beta*I_R1|A}} flows up into the output node and down through $R_2$: $|\mathbf{V}_{out}| = \beta|\mathbf{I}_x|R_2$ = **{{v_v_out|V}}**.

steps.prompt: Tap the nodes that together form a **supernode**.
steps.explanation: $v_2$ connects nodes 2 and 3, neither of which is the reference, so its current is unknown and KCL is written for nodes 2 and 3 together, plus the constraint that $\mathbf{V}_3 - \mathbf{V}_2$ equals the phasor of $v_2$. Node 1 is not part of it: $v_1$ goes to the reference, so it simply fixes $\mathbf{V}_1 = \mathbf{V}_{s1}$. Node 4 is an ordinary node.

steps.title: Mesh currents with phasors
steps.body: Give every window of the circuit a clockwise mesh current $\mathbf{I}_1, \mathbf{I}_2, \dots$ and write KVL around each mesh with impedances. An element shared by two meshes carries $\mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{I}_2$ (in the direction of mesh 1). A current source on an outer branch fixes its mesh current.

steps.prompt: $v_1(t) = {{V1}}\cos({{w}}t)$ V and $v_2(t) = {{V2}}\cos({{w}}t + \theta_2)$ V with $\theta_2$ = {{th2}}°. Mesh currents $\mathbf{I}_1$, $\mathbf{I}_2$ are clockwise.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $\mathbf{I}_1$.
ask.explanation: KVL mesh 1: $(R + Z_C)\mathbf{I}_1 - Z_C\mathbf{I}_2 = \mathbf{V}_1$. Mesh 2 (clockwise enters the + of $v_2$): $-Z_C\mathbf{I}_1 + (Z_C + j\omega L)\mathbf{I}_2 = -\mathbf{V}_2$. With $Z_C$ = −j{{1/(w*C)|Ω}} and $j\omega L$ = j{{w*L|Ω}}: $\mathbf{I}_1$ = **{{I_R1|A}}** ∠ {{I_R1_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $\mathbf{I}_1$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: Solve $(R + Z_C)\mathbf{I}_1 - Z_C\mathbf{I}_2 = \mathbf{V}_1$ and $-Z_C\mathbf{I}_1 + (Z_C + j\omega L)\mathbf{I}_2 = -\mathbf{V}_2$ (Cramer's rule or substitution): $\mathbf{I}_1$ = {{I_R1|A}} ∠ **{{I_R1_ph|°}}**, $\mathbf{I}_2$ = {{I_L1|A}} ∠ {{I_L1_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $\mathbf{I}_2$.
ask.explanation: From the two mesh equations: $\mathbf{I}_2$ = **{{I_L1|A}}** ∠ {{I_L1_ph|°}} (and $\mathbf{I}_1$ = {{I_R1|A}} ∠ {{I_R1_ph|°}}).

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of the current through $C$.
ask.explanation: $C$ is shared: its current (downward) is $\mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{I}_2$ = {{I_R1|A}}∠{{I_R1_ph|°}} − {{I_L1|A}}∠{{I_L1_ph|°}}. Subtract in rectangular form: **{{I_C1|A}}** — not the difference of the amplitudes.

steps.prompt: Which is the KVL equation for mesh 2 (clockwise mesh currents)?
steps.explanation: Going clockwise around mesh 2, the shared $C$ carries $\mathbf{I}_2 - \mathbf{I}_1$, the inductor carries $\mathbf{I}_2$, and the mesh current enters the + terminal of $v_2$, a voltage **rise** of $-\mathbf{V}_2$ as seen by the mesh: $Z_C(\mathbf{I}_2 - \mathbf{I}_1) + j\omega L\,\mathbf{I}_2 + \mathbf{V}_2 = 0$.

steps.prompt: $v_s(t) = {{Vm}}\cos({{w}}t)$ V and $i_s(t) = {{Im*1000}}\cos({{w}}t + \varphi)$ mA with $\varphi$ = {{phi}}°. Mesh currents are clockwise.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $\mathbf{I}_1$.
ask.explanation: The current source is only in mesh 2 and points along it, so $\mathbf{I}_2 = \mathbf{I}_s$. Mesh 1: $R\mathbf{I}_1 + j\omega L(\mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{I}_s) = \mathbf{V}_s$, so $\mathbf{I}_1 = \frac{\mathbf{V}_s + j\omega L\,\mathbf{I}_s}{R + j\omega L}$ = **{{I_R1|A}}** ∠ {{I_R1_ph|°}} ($\omega L$ = {{XL|Ω}}).

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $\mathbf{I}_1$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: $\mathbf{I}_2 = \mathbf{I}_s$ (current source in an outer branch). Then $\mathbf{I}_1 = \frac{\mathbf{V}_s + j\omega L\,\mathbf{I}_s}{R + j\omega L}$ = {{I_R1|A}} ∠ **{{I_R1_ph|°}}**. $C$ does not appear: its current is fixed by the source.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of the current through $L$.
ask.explanation: $\mathbf{I}_L = \mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{I}_2 = \mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{I}_s$ with $\mathbf{I}_1$ = {{I_R1|A}} ∠ {{I_R1_ph|°}} and $\mathbf{I}_s$ = {{Im*1000}}∠{{phi}}° mA: **{{I_L1|A}}**.

steps.prompt: $v_1(t) = {{V1}}\cos({{w}}t)$ V, $v_2(t) = {{V2}}\cos({{w}}t + \theta_2)$ V with $\theta_2$ = {{th2}}°. True or false: the amplitude of the current in $C$ equals $\left||\mathbf{I}_1| - |\mathbf{I}_2|\right|$.
steps.explanation: The shared element carries the **phasor** difference $\mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{I}_2$. Here $\mathbf{I}_1$ = {{I_R1|A}} ∠ {{I_R1_ph|°}} and $\mathbf{I}_2$ = {{I_L1|A}} ∠ {{I_L1_ph|°}}, so $|\mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{I}_2|$ = {{I_C1|A}}, while the difference of the amplitudes is {{abs(I_R1-I_L1)|A}}. They agree only when the two mesh currents are in phase.

steps.prompt: $v_s(t) = {{Vm}}\cos({{w}}t + \theta)$ V with $\theta$ = {{th}}°. Mesh currents are clockwise.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of $\mathbf{I}_2$.
ask.explanation: Mesh 1: $(Z_C + R_2)\mathbf{I}_1 - R_2\mathbf{I}_2 = \mathbf{V}_s$. Mesh 2: $-R_2\mathbf{I}_1 + (R_2 + j\omega L + R_3)\mathbf{I}_2 = 0$, so $\mathbf{I}_1 = \mathbf{I}_2(R_2 + j\omega L + R_3)/R_2$. Substituting: $\mathbf{I}_2$ = **{{I_R3|A}}** ∠ {{I_R3_ph|°}}.

ask.prompt: Find the phase of $\mathbf{I}_2$ in degrees.
ask.explanation: Solving the two mesh equations, $(Z_C + R_2)\mathbf{I}_1 - R_2\mathbf{I}_2 = \mathbf{V}_s$ and $-R_2\mathbf{I}_1 + (R_2 + j\omega L + R_3)\mathbf{I}_2 = 0$: $\mathbf{I}_2$ = {{I_R3|A}} ∠ **{{I_R3_ph|°}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the amplitude of the current through $R_2$.
ask.explanation: $\mathbf{I}_{R_2} = \mathbf{I}_1 - \mathbf{I}_2$ with $\mathbf{I}_1$ = {{I_C1|A}} ∠ {{I_C1_ph|°}} and $\mathbf{I}_2$ = {{I_R3|A}} ∠ {{I_R3_ph|°}}: **{{I_R2|A}}**. Shortcut: $\mathbf{I}_{R_2} = \mathbf{I}_2(j\omega L + R_3)/R_2$.

steps.prompt: Put the steps of phasor mesh analysis in order.
items: Convert sources to phasors and elements to impedances
Assign a clockwise mesh current to every window
Write KVL around each mesh; shared elements carry the difference of two mesh currents
Solve the complex equations for the mesh currents
Find element currents and voltages from the mesh currents
steps.explanation: Mesh analysis is the dual of node analysis: unknown loop currents and KVL instead of node voltages and KCL. A current source in an outer branch removes an unknown (it fixes that mesh current).
